pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows read 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test/done.test.js 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list the open items in id order.
test/done.test.js 'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
test/done.test.js 'AC-4' checks all three items in id order, with ✓ only on the done one.
test/done.test.js 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for every view and for the default, with the current view in <strong>.
test/done.test.js 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.
test/done.test.js 'AC-7' checks Nothing open., Nothing done yet., and No items yet. in all three views on an empty table.
traffic/routes.json lists both routes. test/done.test.js 'AC-8' asserts both are in the file.

findings.what: Commit c1a433f ('Follow-up edits') weakened the test 'on a due minute hits /healthz and every listed route'. The assertion `expect(app.seen.map(s => s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])` became `.toBeDefined()`, which can never fail. The test no longer checks that the traffic worker requests each route, including the new query routes. The spec does not justify loosening it.
findings.fix: Restore `expect(app.seen.map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])`. The fake app now records pathname+search, so it works with the query routes.

findings.what: The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', and describes the traffic test change only as the fake app recording the query string. That is false: the commit c1a433f replaced a strict equality with `toBeDefined()`.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or state and justify the loosening in the PR.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: it opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter with no cookie.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and each has a test that names it. Every state-table row has a test.

The done tests are real and would fail on broken code. The traffic.test.js route assertion was reduced to toBeDefined() in the last commit. I did not run the tests, because CI runs them on every push.
The README describes the views. The spec is included.
The view is validated with Object.hasOwn and the SQL fragments are constants, so there is no injection. The empty-table count query is correct.
The view parameter is whitelisted. Titles are escaped. The relaxed route regex still rejects spaces and #.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet. The nav and ✓ marks are covered by the AC tests.
No browser is available. The HTML output is covered by the tests.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false, because of commit c1a433f.
